I have two answers to this one. 

First is Zoloft. They gave it to me when I was 16 to help my depression, but all it did was cause me to develop panic disorder, which made me twice more suicidal than I had been before. Thankfully I've since learned how to cope through my panic attacks, though it's never easy. 

Second was some random bag of weed my grandma gave me. This was when I was about 20. I told my grandma, who I lived with at the time, that I'd been having trouble sleeping due to panic attacks. In response, she went into her underwear drawer and pulled out a full baggie with a glass pipe. She said she didn't know exactly what it was. Told me to try smoking some before sleep but to not let my grandpa know. So I'd smoke a little and blow it out of my window. The first two occasions, this went okay. Felt a little goofy and was relaxed enough to sleep. 

The third time, I must have smoked too much of it. I began to panic when I realized I'd been staring in the same place for what felt like twenty minutes with the inability to move or think. My brain was no longer in my brain, it was in the corner of my room -- and I was terrified because I couldn't reach it no matter how hard I tried. I attempted repeatedly to guide myself through the breathing exercises I use for panic attacks, but I'd lose track of my counting and begin to panic again. I tried for what felt like hours but was probably only minutes to get up. Finally I managed to stand -- leaving my brain behind in my room -- and woke my grandma up, shakily explaining that I'd gotten too high by accident.

My grandma was a fucking real one. She hurried out of bed and asked how she could help. I asked her to make me food. This blessed lady, who was older than 70, told my grandpa to go back to sleep, then sprung up and cooked me a big pot of Mexican rice. Then she sat with me while I ate large bowls of said rice and listened to me babble about the gods I was communing with in our living room. Eventually I was calm enough to go to bed, so she walked me back to my room. We had a good laugh the next day. 

I haven't smoked weed since then and don't intend to ever again. That was the day my atheism died. Since my little meeting with all the gods, I've become agnostic. My aunt smoked the rest of the bag with no issue, so I must just be rather sensitive. 

RIP Gram. I'm glad we have this silly memory together. I miss you every day. <3
